Information on diet data

Childhood diet at 4 years (1950) was collected as follows:

  • a 24-hour maternal recall of all meals consumed was completed

for 98% of cohort members. (Prynne et al,1999).

  • Nutrient intakes were later calculated using period and age-specific food portion sizes and nutrient databases.

Adult diet data were collected as follows:

At the adult ages, all food and drink consumed both at home and away was recorded in the diaries using household measures and estimating portion sizes according to detailed guidance notes and photographs provided at the beginning of the diary. The 1989 and 1999 diaries were coded using the in-house program DIDO. This program is designed around a hierarchical food menu that offers nearly 2000 foods. A food item, having been selected can be entered as the portion size corresponding to that described in the diary. The output file from the previous coding of the 1982 diaries was converted into a form compatible with the later DIDO output files. Foods (in grams) and nutrient intakes ( units as specified in the variable labels) for all four assessments were calculated using the in-house suite of programs based on McCance and Widdowson’s The Composition of Foods, 4th edition and supplements. The dietary data have been processed by MRC-Human Nutrition Research. Intakes of 83 food items and nutrients for each diary day are available at ages 36, 43, and 53.

1982 (age 36)

  • 2 day recall followed by 5 day diet diary at age 36

1989 (age 43)

  • 2 day recall followed by 5 day diet diary at age 43

1999 (age 53)

  • 5 day diet diary at age 53 .

Notes:

  1. The variables for 1982 and 1989 have been indexed by the maximum number of repeat records which is 7.
  2. The variables for 1999 datasets have been indexed by the maximum number of repeat records which is 5.
